lines: Eyebrow: Approach

Body: Zeitwerk is a consulting and implementation firm based in Vaughan, Ontario. We design, build and maintain the automation behind business operations across Toronto and the GTA, from the first audit to the system running in production.

Headline: Six stages, in order.

02 Solution design: Body: We architect a system that fits your business, your existing tools and the volume you expect.
You get: A design you can read before any code is written.
03 System build: Body: We write the automation and integrations, including the error handling for when inputs are wrong or a service is down.
You get: Working software, built against your real data.
04 Integration: Body: We connect the tools you already run, such as your CRM, ERP and email, so they behave as one system instead of several.
You get: No new app for your team to learn unless one is needed.
05 Testing and QA: Body: We stress-test the edge cases before launch, so the system runs reliably without someone watching it.
You get: A launch that does not depend on luck.
06 Launch and scale: Body: We deploy, monitor real usage and keep tuning as your business and your volume change.
You get: Ongoing support from the people who built it.

lines: Eyebrow: 01 / AI receptionists
Headline: Every call answered. Including the 11 p.m. ones.
Subhead: An AI receptionist picks up immediately, speaks naturally, qualifies the caller, books the appointment and sends anything complex to the right person, with a full transcript in your inbox.
Primary CTA: Book a free consultation
Secondary CTA: info@zeitwerk.ca
Section label: The problem
Headline: The phone keeps ringing after five.

Body: A missed call is a lead that dials your competitor next, a tenant whose small problem becomes a large one, or a customer who gives up. When the front desk is stretched, or nobody can staff the phones after hours, the calls still come in. They just go unanswered.
List label: Sound familiar?
- Calls go to voicemail at peak hours, and most callers never leave a message.
- After-hours calls are lost, or they wake whoever is on call for something routine.
- Reception spends the day answering the same handful of questions.
- Messages get taken, and the details get lost before anyone follows up.
- You pay an answering service that reads a script and cannot resolve anything.
Closer: None of this is a staffing problem. It is a workflow that was never designed to scale, and that is what we fix.
Section label: How it works
Intro: We understand the workflow first, then engineer the automation around it.
01 Map your call flow: Who calls, why, what they need and what should happen in each case, from booking requests to real emergencies.
02 Design the voice and rules: How the receptionist speaks, the questions it asks to qualify callers and the exact escalation rules for anything it should not handle alone.
03 Build and integrate: We connect it to your calendar, CRM or ticketing tools, so calls end as booked appointments and logged requests instead of sticky notes.
04 Test, launch and tune: We stress-test edge cases before launch, then review real calls and refine the prompts and routing as the business changes.
Section label: Built for
Headline: Businesses where the phone is the front door.
- Property managers fielding tenant calls at all hours
- Trades and home-service companies losing jobs to unanswered phones
- Clinics, law offices and professional practices with an overloaded front desk
- Any GTA business that cannot afford a missed call
Label: Case study
Title: Intelligent Collections Engine
Line: The same voice technology runs our rent collections system: two-way SMS and AI voice that cut manual calls by 70%. Agents now handle only escalated cases.

Q: Will callers know they are talking to an AI?

A: We recommend that it says so. Callers care far more about being helped right away than about who answers. The receptionist handles routine matters completely and hands off cleanly when a person is needed.
Q: What happens when the AI cannot handle a call?

A: We design the escalation rules with you before launch. It can transfer to a person, take a structured message, send an urgent alert or book a callback. Every call produces a transcript, so nothing is lost.
Q: Does this replace my receptionist?
A: Usually it protects them. The AI takes after-hours calls, overflow and repeat questions, so your team can focus on the conversations that need a person.
Q: What does an AI receptionist cost in Toronto?

A: It depends on call volume and the systems we connect to, so we scope each project individually. Start with a free consultation. We will audit your call flow and give you a clear recommendation and quote before you commit.

lines: Eyebrow: 05 / Document intake
Headline: The end of manual re-keying.

Subhead: The pipeline reads what arrives (PDFs, scans, photos, forms), extracts the fields that matter, checks them and writes them straight into your systems. People review the exceptions, not the pile.
Primary CTA: Book a free consultation
Secondary CTA: info@zeitwerk.ca
Section label: The problem
Headline: Someone is still typing numbers off a PDF.
Body: Invoices, receipts, applications and inspection forms, each one re-keyed by hand. Each one is a chance for a typo, and the minutes add up to someone's entire job.
List label: The re-keying tax
- Staff spend hours a week copying data from documents into software.
- Typos and missed fields surface weeks later as accounting or compliance problems.
- Documents arrive by email, portal and paper, and pile up in all three.
- Backlogs grow every time volume spikes or someone is away.
- The people doing the re-keying were hired to do something more useful.
Closer: None of this is a staffing problem. It is a workflow that was never designed to scale, and that is what we fix.
Section label: How it works
01 Inventory your documents: What arrives, in what formats, from where, and which fields need to end up in which system.
02 Build the extraction pipeline: AI extraction reads each document, including scans and phone photos, and validation rules catch anything that looks wrong.
03 Connect your systems: Extracted data goes straight into your accounting platform, database or line-of-business software, with no copy and paste in between.
04 Route the exceptions: Documents the system cannot read with confidence go to a review queue with the uncertain fields highlighted, so people handle judgment instead of volume.
Section label: Built for
Headline: Paper-heavy operations.
- Finance teams processing invoices, receipts and expense claims
- Property and field operations handling inspections and work orders
- Offices running application, onboarding or intake forms
- Any GTA business where documents arrive faster than they get processed
Q: What kinds of documents can it handle?
A: Invoices, receipts, forms, applications, inspection reports and most other business documents, as native PDFs, scans or phone photos. If a person can read it, it is usually a candidate.
Q: How accurate is the extraction?

A: Very accurate on well-structured documents, and we do not rely on trust alone. Validation rules and confidence thresholds send anything questionable to a person. In one project listed on our projects page, receipt extraction reached 95%+ accuracy with automatic G/L coding.
Q: Where does the extracted data go?
A: Wherever it needs to: accounting software, ERP, a database or a spreadsheet. We build the integration so data lands in the system your team already uses.
Q: What happens to the original documents?
A: They are filed automatically, named consistently and stored where you want them, so the source is always one click from the record it produced.

lines: Eyebrow: 04 / Inbox triage
Headline: An inbox that sorts itself.
Subhead: Every incoming message is classified, prioritized, routed to its owner and drafted for review. The inbox turns into a queue of decisions instead of a wall of unread mail.
Primary CTA: Book a free consultation
Secondary CTA: info@zeitwerk.ca
Section label: The problem
Headline: Shared inboxes fail quietly.

Body: A few hundred messages a day and nothing looks broken. The urgent request is just buried under newsletters, the customer has followed up twice, and your best people spend the first hour of every morning deciding what to read.
List label: How high-volume inboxes fail
- Urgent messages sit unseen behind routine ones for hours.
- Nobody is sure who owns a message, so everyone answers or no one does.
- Your most experienced people spend mornings sorting instead of solving.
- The same questions get hand-typed answers dozens of times a week.
- Follow-ups slip because nothing tracks what is still waiting on a reply.
Closer: None of this is a staffing problem. It is a workflow that was never designed to scale, and that is what we fix.
Section label: How it works
01 Learn your mail: We study what you actually receive and define the categories, priorities and owners that match how your team works.
02 Classify and route: Each message is categorized, prioritized and assigned as it arrives. Urgent items are flagged the moment they land.
03 Draft the replies: For routine mail the system drafts a response in your voice for a person to approve, edit or send. Fully automatic replies run only where you switch them on.
04 Track and improve: Nothing closes until it is handled. We review the misses and keep tuning, so accuracy improves with use.
Section label: Built for
Headline: Inboxes that never stop.
- Property management offices buried in tenant email
- Customer service desks without a full ticketing system
- Operations teams running the business from a shared mailbox
- Executives who need a short brief instead of a thousand unread messages
Q: What if it files something incorrectly?

A: We set confidence thresholds, so messages the system is unsure about go to a person instead of being guessed at. Misfiled items are reviewed and fed back in, and the system gets sharper the longer it runs.
Q: Will it send email without us knowing?
A: Only if you switch that on for specific, well-defined message types. The default is drafts for review: a person approves everything until you are comfortable expanding it.
Q: Does it work with Outlook and Gmail?
A: Yes. We build on Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace, using your existing mailboxes and permissions instead of moving you to a new tool.
Q: What about confidentiality?
A: Before anything goes live, we walk you through what the system reads, where the data flows and what is stored. We design within your existing email platform and access policies.

meta.meta_description: Polite, persistent, automated follow-up on unpaid invoices by email, SMS and AI voice. Collections automation for Toronto and GTA businesses.

lines: Eyebrow: 03 / Invoice follow-up
Headline: Get paid without chasing.
Subhead: Personalized reminders go out by email, SMS and AI voice, paced and escalated on purpose, with every touch tracked. Your team steps in only when a case needs a person.
Primary CTA: Book a free consultation
Secondary CTA: info@zeitwerk.ca
Section label: The problem
Headline: Unpaid usually means busy, not unwilling.
Body: Every week an invoice sits unpaid, cash flow tightens and the follow-up call gets more awkward. So it gets postponed, and the problem compounds.
List label: The cost of not chasing
- Receivables age because follow-up depends on someone remembering.
- Every customer gets the same generic reminder, whatever their history.
- Staff dread collection calls, so they happen late or not at all.
- Nobody can say which invoices were chased, when, or with what result.
- Cash flow suffers even though the work is done and the customer is willing to pay.
Closer: None of this is a staffing problem. It is a workflow that was never designed to scale, and that is what we fix.
Section label: How it works
01 Connect your receivables: We connect to your invoicing or accounting system, so the automation always knows what is outstanding, overdue or promised.
02 Design the cadence: Together we set tone and pacing: a friendly nudge, a firm reminder, then escalation. Different customers and amounts can follow different paths.
03 Automate across channels: Reminders go out by email, two-way SMS or a natural AI voice call, written for the customer and the invoice instead of one blast for everyone.
04 Escalate only what matters: Disputes, hardship cases and silence past your threshold go to your team with full context. The rest resolves without them.
Section label: Built for
Headline: Businesses with real receivables.
- Property managers and landlords collecting rent at scale
- Trades and contractors whose net-30 invoices drift to net-90
- Agencies and professional services chasing retainers
- Any GTA business where receivables outrun the time to collect them
Label: Case study
Title: Intelligent Collections Engine
Line: Two-way SMS and AI voice with GPT-personalized messages per resident. 98% SMS delivery and 70% fewer manual calls.
CTA: Read the case study
Link: /projects/intelligent-collections-engine
Q: Won't automated collections annoy my customers?

A: Done crudely, yes. That is why we set tone and pacing with you before anything goes out. A polite, well-spaced, personal reminder is far less irritating than a tense phone call after ninety days of silence, and customers respond to it.
Q: Which channels can it use?
A: Email, two-way SMS and natural AI voice calls, in whatever mix suits your customers. Messages adapt to the customer and the invoice instead of following one script.
Q: When does a person get involved?
A: Whenever you decide: disputes, promised payments that lapse, sensitive accounts or balances past a threshold you set. Your team gets the full history, so the conversation starts informed.
Q: Does it work with our accounting software?
A: We connect to the invoicing and accounting tools you already run, so balances stay in sync and a payment stops the reminders automatically.

meta.meta_description: Turn inbound requests into accurate, branded quotes in minutes instead of days. Zeitwerk builds quoting automation for Toronto and GTA businesses.

lines: Eyebrow: 02 / Quote automation
Headline: Quotes out in minutes, not days.
Subhead: The system reads each request, applies your real pricing rules and drafts a branded quote ready for one-click review. Routine work can go out on its own. Anything unusual waits for a person.
Primary CTA: Book a free consultation
Secondary CTA: info@zeitwerk.ca
Section label: The problem
Headline: The first good quote usually wins.
Body: If a request sits in your inbox for three days while a competitor replies within the hour, the job is gone before you open the pricing spreadsheet.
List label: Where quoting breaks down
- Pricing lives in one person's head or in a spreadsheet nobody else trusts.
- Requests arrive by email, phone and web form, and some fall through.
- Two staff quote the same job two different ways.
- Sent quotes get followed up when someone remembers, so warm leads expire.
- Busy season creates a quoting backlog exactly when you can least afford one.
Closer: None of this is a staffing problem. It is a workflow that was never designed to scale, and that is what we fix.
Section label: How it works
01 Capture your pricing logic: Rates, materials, margins, minimums and the exceptions. We write down how you actually price work and turn it into explicit rules.
02 Build the drafting engine: The system reads each request from email, web form or call notes, pulls out the details that matter, applies your rules and assembles a complete quote.
03 Add review and approval: You set the guardrails. Routine quotes can send automatically or wait for one-click approval, and anything unusual is clearly flagged.
04 Automate the follow-up: Sent quotes get polite, scheduled follow-ups until they are accepted, declined or expired.
Section label: Built for
Headline: Teams that compete on response time.
- Trades, contractors and home-service companies
- Wholesale, distribution and equipment suppliers
- Professional services pricing scoped engagements
- Any GTA business that loses work to slower replies
Q: How does it keep quotes accurate?

A: It only applies pricing rules you have approved. Anything outside normal parameters, such as unusual scope, missing information or non-standard pricing, goes to a person for review instead of being sent blind.
Q: Our jobs are custom. Can this still work?
A: Yes, and that is the usual case. The system drafts the structured majority of each quote and flags the judgment calls for you, which turns a process of days into minutes of review.
Q: Does it connect to our CRM or accounting software?
A: We build against the CRM, accounting and email tools you already use, so accepted quotes flow into your existing pipeline instead of another disconnected app.
Q: What does quoting automation cost?

A: It depends on how complex your pricing is and what we connect to. We scope every project individually. Book a free consultation and we will map your quoting workflow and give you a clear recommendation first.

lines: Eyebrow: 06 / Reporting and dashboards
Headline: Reports that build themselves.
Subhead: We pull data from the tools you already run, keep it live in a dashboard your team will use and send scheduled reports on time. Same numbers, no assembly.
Primary CTA: Book a free consultation
Secondary CTA: info@zeitwerk.ca
Section label: The problem
Headline: The report is out of date before the meeting.

Body: Someone opens six spreadsheets, exports from four systems and spends Friday afternoon building a report that is stale by Monday. Each copy-paste error makes people trust the numbers a little less.
List label: Signs your reporting is running you
- Reports take hours of manual export, copy and paste every week or month.
- By the time leadership sees the numbers, they are days old.
- Each department keeps its own spreadsheet and its own version of the truth.
- One person knows how the report is built, and it stops when they are away.
- Errors surface in meetings, and the discussion turns to the data instead of the decision.
Closer: None of this is a staffing problem. It is a workflow that was never designed to scale, and that is what we fix.
Section label: How it works
01 Find the real sources: We trace every number in your current reports back to its source system and mark where manual steps and errors creep in.
02 Automate the pipeline: Data flows from your CRM, accounting, operations and spreadsheet tools into one consistent model that stays current.
03 Build dashboards people use: Drill-down for the people who dig, and clean executive views for the people who decide.
04 Deliver on schedule: Weekly and monthly reports generate and send themselves, to inboxes or as PDFs, without anyone assembling anything.
Section label: Built for
Headline: Decision-makers tired of stale numbers.
- Executives running portfolios, branches or several entities
- Operations leaders reporting KPIs every week
- Finance teams building month-end packs by hand
- Any GTA business making decisions on days-old data
Label: Case study
Title: Property Intelligence Platform
Line: A real-time executive dashboard across 171 properties and 17,968 units that replaced manual portfolio reporting and saves roughly 40 hours a week.
CTA: Read the case study
Link: /projects/property-intelligence-platform
Q: What data sources can you connect?

A: Most modern business systems: CRMs, accounting platforms, operations software, databases, and the spreadsheets and email exports you rely on today. If the data exists somewhere, we can usually automate its path into the report.
Q: Do we need a data warehouse?

A: Not necessarily. We size the architecture to the problem, and many businesses get live, trustworthy reporting without heavy infrastructure. If your volume calls for more, we will tell you and design for it.
Q: Can we still get reports by email or PDF?
A: Yes. The same pipeline can feed a live dashboard and email a formatted PDF pack on whatever schedule you set.
Q: What does reporting automation cost?
A: It depends on how many sources we connect and how complex the reporting is. Book a free consultation and we will audit your current reporting and show you what to automate first.
